skill.name: requesting-code-review
skill.description: Create a structured request for AI-assisted code review of a pull request, merge request, branch, or commit range.
skill.summary: Builds a consistent code review brief with scope, Git range, severity guidance, and merge readiness criteria.
skill.author: CodingCossack

content.value_statement: Code review requests often miss context, scope, or acceptance criteria. This skill creates a structured brief for Claude, Codex, or Claude Code reviewers.
actual_capabilities: Provides a repeatable workflow for collecting base and head Git SHAs.
Supplies a reusable code-reviewer prompt template with required context fields.
Guides reviewers to compare implementation against requirements or plans.
Separates findings into Critical, Important, and Minor severity groups.
Requires file and line references for each reported issue.
Asks for a clear merge readiness assessment with concise reasoning.
limitations: It does not perform the code review without an AI reviewer or subagent.
It depends on accurate Git SHAs and clear implementation context.
It cannot guarantee detection of every defect or security issue.
It may need adaptation for repositories that do not use Git workflows.

use_cases.title: Prepare Pull Request Reviews
use_cases.description: Create a complete review brief before requesting feedback on a pull request.

use_cases.title: Review Plan-Based Work
use_cases.description: Ask an AI reviewer to compare completed tasks against a plan or requirements document.

use_cases.title: Standardize Merge Checks
use_cases.description: Use consistent severity levels, test expectations, and readiness criteria before merging changes.

prompt_templates.title: Basic Review Request
prompt_templates.scenario: Use after finishing a small branch or pull request.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a code review request for my current branch. Include what changed, the Git range, tests run, and a merge readiness question.

prompt_templates.title: Requirements Comparison Review
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when changes must match a written task or specification.
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare a review brief that compares my implementation against these requirements: [paste requirements]. Highlight risk areas and acceptance criteria.

prompt_templates.title: Subagent Review Dispatch
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when delegating the review to a dedicated AI reviewer.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the code-reviewer template to review this change range. Focus on correctness, architecture, tests, security, and production readiness.

prompt_templates.title: Release Readiness Gate
prompt_templates.scenario: Use before merging higher-risk production changes.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an advanced review request for a release gate. Include scope, non-goals, migrations, rollback concerns, test evidence, and clear pass criteria.

output_examples.input: A developer finished a branch that adds account verification and wants an AI review before merge.
output: The response frames the implementation scope and expected behavior.
It asks the reviewer to inspect the selected Git range against the requirements.
It requests Critical, Important, and Minor findings with a merge readiness verdict.

output_examples.input: An engineering lead completed several plan tasks and wants review before starting the next batch.
output: The response identifies the plan section, completed work, and review boundaries.
It emphasizes tests, architecture, missing requirements, and production risks.
It directs the reviewer to explain each issue with impact and a fix path.

output_examples.input: A quality team wants a consistent checklist for merge request review requests.
output: The response creates a standard request format with context, scope, and acceptance criteria.
It asks for specific file references and a clear readiness decision.

best_practices: Provide the reviewer with the exact Git range and the requirement source.
List tests that were run and tests that were intentionally deferred.
Act on Critical and Important findings before continuing dependent work.
anti_patterns: Do not request review without explaining what changed and why.
Do not treat a vague approval as a substitute for issue-based review.
Do not ignore valid Important findings before merging production code.

faq.question: What does this skill help me create?
faq.answer: It helps create a structured request for reviewing code changes before merge.

faq.question: Does it run the code review itself?
faq.answer: No. It prepares the brief and template for Claude, Codex, Claude Code, or another reviewer.

faq.question: What information should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide what changed, the requirements, the base and head commits, tests run, and known risk areas.

faq.question: Can it support pull requests and merge requests?
faq.answer: Yes. The workflow fits pull requests, merge requests, branch reviews, and commit-range reviews.

faq.question: How are findings organized?
faq.answer: The template asks for Critical, Important, and Minor findings plus a merge readiness assessment.

faq.question: Is it safe for sensitive repositories?
faq.answer: Use normal repository security controls. The skill does not require network access or secret handling.
